The earlier pages represented discrete probability with a [probability mass function](probability-mass-functions.qmd) and continuous probability with a [probability density function](probability-density-functions.qmd). Must we switch representations every time we move between the two kinds of variable? A cumulative distribution function gives one threshold-based representation that applies to both.

A [**cumulative distribution function**](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-intro.html), abbreviated [**CDF**](https://bruno.nicenboim.me/bayescogsci/ch-intro.html), records the probability at or below every threshold:

$$
F_X:\mathbb R\to[0,1],
\qquad
F_X(x)\equiv\mathbb{P}(X\leq x).
$$

The function accumulates probability from the lower end of the support through the threshold $x$.

We compute the empirical CDF (ECDF) of the [Hillenbrand adult-men /i/ durations](continuous-random-variables.qmd#hillenbrand-vowel-duration). One row is one token from one adult male speaker.

```{r}
#| label: load-hillenbrand-cdf
library(ggplot2)

vowels <- read.csv(
  "data/hillenbrand/vowels-complete.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
adult_i <- subset(vowels, speaker_type == "man" & vowel == "i")
duration_ecdf <- ecdf(adult_i$duration_ms)
q25 <- unname(quantile(adult_i$duration_ms, 0.25, type = 1))
q75 <- unname(quantile(adult_i$duration_ms, 0.75, type = 1))
f_q25 <- duration_ecdf(q25)
f_q75 <- duration_ecdf(q75)
middle_probability <- f_q75 - f_q25

stopifnot(
  nrow(adult_i) == 45L,
  !anyDuplicated(adult_i$speaker_id),
  q25 <= q75,
  abs(f_q25 - mean(adult_i$duration_ms <= q25)) < 1e-12,
  abs(f_q75 - mean(adult_i$duration_ms <= q75)) < 1e-12,
  abs(middle_probability -
        mean(adult_i$duration_ms > q25 & adult_i$duration_ms <= q75)) < 1e-12
)

c(q25_ms = q25, F_q25 = f_q25,
  q75_ms = q75, F_q75 = f_q75,
  probability_q25_open_q75_closed = middle_probability)
```

## Constructing a discrete CDF

For a discrete variable,

$$
F_X(x)
=\sum_{\substack{x'\in\operatorname{cod}(X)\\x'\leq x}}p_X(x').
$$

The ECDF treats each observed duration record as a discrete outcome with equal mass. It consequently increases in jumps at recorded values, even though we may model the underlying acoustic quantity as continuous.

```{r}
#| label: plot-hillenbrand-ecdf
#| fig-cap: "Empirical cumulative distribution of adult-men /i/ duration. Rug marks show the observed tokens."
ggplot(adult_i, aes(duration_ms)) +
  stat_ecdf(geom = "step", color = "steelblue") +
  geom_rug(color = "grey") +
  labs(x = "Vowel duration (ms)", y = "Empirical cumulative probability") +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12)
```

## Accumulating a continuous density

For an absolutely continuous variable with density $f_X$, the same definition is represented by area:

$$
F_X(x)=\int_{-\infty}^{x}f_X(x')\,\mathrm dx'.
$$

The operation changes from summing masses to integrating density, but the interpretation remains $\mathbb{P}(X\leq x)$.

The probability in an interval above $a$ and at or below $b$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{P}(a<X\leq b)
&=F_X(b)-F_X(a).
\end{aligned}
$$

Using the empirical first and third quartiles as the thresholds, the displayed code returns `r sprintf("%.3f", middle_probability)` for $\mathbb{P}(q_{.25}<D\leq q_{.75})$. Ties at the lower threshold matter because the event is open on the left and closed on the right.

## Reading the threshold direction

The definition always uses the lower tail:

$$
F_X(x)\equiv\mathbb{P}(X\leq x).
$$

An upper-tail probability follows by complementation:

$$
\mathbb{P}(X>x)=1-F_X(x).
$$

Thus the empirical probability above `r q75` ms is `r sprintf("%.3f", 1 - f_q75)`. This value comes from the observed durations; it is not a claim about all American English /i/ productions.

## Check your understanding

1. Use `duration_ecdf()` to compute the empirical probability at or below the observed median duration.
2. Verify the upper-tail probability above `q75` by averaging a logical condition over `adult_i$duration_ms`.
3. Why does the ECDF jump even when duration is modeled as an underlying continuous quantity?
4. Change the interval to $[q_{.25},q_{.75}]$. Which records are added relative to the interval used above?

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. At the observed median of 240 ms, `duration_ecdf(240) = 23/45 = 0.511111`. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
2. The direct upper-tail calculation is `mean(adult_i$duration_ms > 268) = 10/45 = 0.222222`, equal to $1-F(268)$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
3. The ECDF jumps because it assigns equal positive mass to each of the 45 recorded tokens, even if the underlying duration process is modeled continuously. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->
4. Changing $(q_{.25},q_{.75}]$ to $[q_{.25},q_{.75}]$ adds the one record at 219 ms, increasing the interval probability by $1/45$. <!-- dqr-allow: empirical-answer -->

</details>

The CDF describes probability through every threshold. The [next page](expected-values.qmd) compresses a complete distribution into one probability-weighted center.
